description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the perlfunc INDEX battery (pf-lc-uc-etc).  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/angles/perlfunc/ + scratchpad lcbytes.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main:

    print lc("ÀB")            (file is UTF-8, NO `use utf8`)     perl: bytes C3 80 62 ("Àb" intact)   PCL: E3 80 62 (invalid UTF-8)
    "\xc3\x85" =~ /\w/                                            perl: no match                       PCL: match
    uc("å a"), ucfirst("élan")                                    same in both (lowercase lead bytes C3 have no Latin-1 uppercase image that differs... only by luck)

perl's rule: a string WITHOUT the UTF-8 flag gets ASCII-only case mapping and ASCII-only \w/\d/\s, unless `use feature 'unicode_strings'` (in `use v5.12`+), `use locale`, or /u.  PCL has no per-scalar flag (#1389 ruling, not-supported.md "The per-scalar UTF-8 flag") and applies Unicode rules to every character, so a program that reads UTF-8 BYTES and lowercases them (grep -i style tools, log mungers, any script written before `use utf8` was habit) emits corrupt bytes -- silently.  not-supported.md's Unicode section claims "without the pragma, high bytes stay Latin-1 (byte semantics), matching Perl" -- true for length/substr, FALSE for casing and character classes.
FABLE DESIGN NEEDED (do not start coding): without a per-scalar flag the choice is per PROGRAM or per OPERATION.  Candidate: a compile-time mode bit -- a file with no `use utf8`, no `unicode_strings`/`use v5.12+`, no `use open`/`:encoding`/`Encode`/`utf8::decode` anywhere is a BYTE PROGRAM and gets ASCII-only casing + classes for chars 128-255 (chars > 255 can only come from decoding, so they keep Unicode rules).  Cost/risk to measure: what the sweep + companion do under that rule (lib/ shims that decode?), and the converse error (a decoded "É" in a program that decodes via a module PCL cannot see).  Until designed: a not-supported.md correction is owed (the sentence above is wrong as written).


=== THE DESIGN (Fable, s494, 2026-09-21) -- an agent builds PHASE 1 from this section; PHASE 2 is a measurement that comes back to Fable ===
PERL'S RULE, PROBED (5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2092/rules.pl = the acceptance table, rules.perl.out = the expected answers).  perl names the four regimes itself -- the regex modifiers /d /u /a /l -- and the same split governs case mapping:
  * /d ("depends", the default when NO `unicode_strings` feature is in scope): a char 128-255 gets Unicode rules only if the STRING carries the UTF-8 flag.  P1 lc(raw bytes C3 80 62) = C3 80 62; P5 lc(chr(0xC9)) = C9 (unflagged: NOT folded); P4 lc(decoded U+00C0) = E0; P6 lc(upgraded chr(0xC9)) = E9; P9 raw bytes `\w` = www-- ; P10 decoded = wwww; P11 `s/\W+/_/g` on raw "café x" = "caf_x"; P12 "\xC9" =~ /\xE9/i = no.
  * /u (`use feature 'unicode_strings'` = `use v5.12`+, or an explicit /u): Unicode rules for EVERY string.  P2 lc(raw bytes) = E3 80 62 -- PERL ITSELF corrupts raw UTF-8 bytes here; P3 lc(chr(0xC9)) = E9; P13/P14 bytes `\w` = wwww-.
  * /a: ASCII-only classes even for a decoded string.  P15 = www-.
  * /l (`use locale`): not supported, unchanged.
WHAT PCL DOES TODAY = /u EVERYWHERE, for every string: exact at a unicode_strings site, and at a /d site it is right for DECODED text and CORRUPTS raw UTF-8 bytes: P1 (E3 80 62 = invalid UTF-8), P11 ("caf\xC3_x" = invalid UTF-8: `\W` eats the continuation byte and leaves the lead byte), P9, P12; P5 folds where perl does not (benign).  P15: `/a` is NOT HONOURED (decoded é matches \w) -- a plain bug, fixed in phase 1 because it is the SAME class table the /d work needs (rule 11).
THE MISSING DATUM is the per-scalar flag, and only for chars 128-255 (a char > 255 implies flagged).  #1389 ruled there is no flag; so a /d site needs an APPROXIMATION of it.  Three candidates, with their error sets:
  (U) today: Unicode always.  Error: raw UTF-8 BYTES at a /d site -> CORRUPT OUTPUT.  Population: every script that munges UTF-8 text without decoding it -- the majority of scripts ever written.
  (S) static, per file: no `use utf8` and no unicode_strings => ASCII rules for 128-255.  Error: DECODED text at such a site -- a script that decodes through a layer / Encode but has no `use utf8`, and above all an OLD MODULE (no pragmas: most of CPAN) called with decoded text by a modern script: `\w` stops matching é inside the module.  Non-corrupting but common.
  (D) DATA SNIFF, per operation: at a /d site, a string whose chars 128-255 ALL sit in well-formed UTF-8 sequences (and no char > 255) is treated as UNFLAGGED BYTES (ASCII rules for 128-255); anything else as flagged (Unicode rules).  Decoded text essentially never forms valid UTF-8 byte sequences (it needs a lead-range char C2-F4 followed by a continuation-range char 80-BF for EVERY high char: "Ã©"), raw UTF-8 text always does.  Errors: (i) decoded text that is accidentally all-valid (e.g. "CAFÉ»": C9 BB) -> not folded: RARE and non-corrupting; (ii) genuine LATIN-1 bytes / `chr(0xC9)` at a /d site -> folded where perl does not (P5): non-corrupting, and what the author of a Latin-1 script wanted.  (D) removes the corrupting class and keeps old-module + modern-script working.
RULING (Fable; the USER may overrule -- it is visible semantics): **the lexical half is perl-exact and the flag is approximated by (D)**: a site under `unicode_strings` (the feature-at-position mechanism #455 / #364 already built: `use v5.12`+, `use feature 'unicode_strings'`, `:5.12`+ bundles, inherited into a string eval through the FEATURES list) or a regex with /u gets Unicode rules for every string = today's behaviour, unchanged; /a gets ASCII classes; every other site is /d and applies (D).  not-supported.md's Unicode section is corrected in the same commit: the sentence "without the pragma, high bytes stay Latin-1 (byte semantics), matching Perl" becomes the rule above + the two (D) error sets, under "The per-scalar UTF-8 flag".

PHASE 1 (one agent, about a day) -- CASE MAPPING + /a: lc uc lcfirst ucfirst fc and the `\L \U \l \u \F` interpolation escapes (find the ONE runtime function they share; if there are two copies that is the first finding).  The mapping loop already visits every char, so (D) costs one validation pass ONLY for a string that contains a char >= 128 -- pure ASCII keeps today's path (the bench rows `textproc`, `strcat` and whatever row lowercases must not move: FLAG > 1 %).  ONE helper `%p-bytes-look-utf8-p` (strict well-formedness: no overlongs, no surrogates, <= U+10FFFF, a truncated tail = NOT valid), used by nothing else yet.  EMISSION: the site's regime reaches the runtime as data, not as a new function family: the builder chooses between a second exported entry (`p-lc` = /d, a `-u` twin at unicode_strings sites) and a keyword -- whichever makes `tools/corpus-diff.pl` ONE explainable class; files with no `use v5.12`+ must be emission-IDENTICAL.  /a: the regex translator's class table gains the ASCII-restricted variants (`\w \d \s \b` + POSIX classes + /i folding limited to ASCII) selected by the modifier; `/aa` = /a plus no ASCII/non-ASCII /i crossing (K vs KELVIN SIGN) -- implement /a, DIE-announce on /aa only if it cannot be had for free (rule 12 boundary: a modifier that changes VALUES must not be silently ignored -- and today /a IS silently ignored).
  BAR: rules.pl rows P1 P4 P5(*) P6 P7 P8 P2 P3 P15 (* P5 stays a DOCUMENTED divergence under (D)); a new Pl/t file with the byte rows written as `\x` escapes (no literal high bytes in the test file, so the test does not depend on how the FILE is decoded -- #2192); the s493 probe `pf-lc-uc-etc`; corpus-diff explained as one class + gen bump + artifacts; full sweep; companion `op/lc.t op/uc*.t re/` legs (`--jobs 1`; op/lc.t is the file that knows these rules row by row -- read its movers in BOTH directions); ir-spec's string-ops section states the regime rule normatively + ONE example.
PHASE 2 -- REGEX AT /d SITES: MEASURE, THEN FABLE RULES.  `\w \d \s \b`, POSIX classes and /i on chars 128-255.  (D) per match means knowing whether the SUBJECT looks like UTF-8 bytes: an O(n) scan per match operation -- ~0.3-1 ns/char, i.e. +5-10 % on a regex-heavy row over 80-char lines, and QUADRATIC on an m//g loop over one big subject unless the verdict is cached with the iteration state (#477's lesson).  Do NOT build it blind.  The measurement an agent brings back: (1) the share of regex SITES in the four populations that are /d AND contain an affected construct (the translator can count them); (2) an experiment switch `PCL_REGEX_D=unicode|ascii|sniff` (three class-table selections; `sniff` with the per-subject cache) and the row movement of sweep + companion `re/` + the CPAN board under each, BOTH directions, plus the bench A/B of `sniff` on `regexg` / `subste` / `textproc`; (3) the rows P9 P10 P11 P12 P13 P14 under each.  Fable picks the regime from that table.  Until then regex stays (U) and not-supported.md says so explicitly (P11's shape -- `s/\W+/_/g` over undecoded UTF-8 leaves lead bytes behind -- is the sentence a user needs).
RELATED, FOUND WHILE PROBING: #2192 (`use utf8` detected textually -- a comment or POD mentioning it decodes the whole file; it corrupted this task's own probe labels).


=== USER RULING s494 (2026-09-21) ===
The design's RULING -- the lexical half perl-exact, the missing per-scalar flag approximated at /d sites by the DATA SNIFF (well-formed UTF-8 high chars = bytes = ASCII rules), the static per-file rule rejected -- was put to the USER as a visible-semantics decision: **"Decision 1 sounds good to me."**  APPROVED; PHASE 1 can be built from the design as written (brief ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/s494u/prompt.md).

REGIME :u is emitted only at unicode_strings sites (Pl::Parser::unicode_strings_regions_of, inherited by string eval); every other site is /d = the DATA SNIFF (%p-bytes-look-utf8-p).  /d emission byte-identical: corpus-diff moves ONE file, perl-tests/lc.t, `(p-lc x)` -> `(p-lc x :u)`.
* /a and /aa IMPLEMENTED in the one rewrite scan (%pcl-rewrite-scan: rxs-a/astack, %pcl-rx-ascii-escape-text, inline (?a) (?^...) tracked; qr stringifies a aa u l).

Error (i) = decoded text that is valid UTF-8 as bytes is not folded.
* Guards Pl/t/case-regime-01.t (37 rows; 22 fail on 209e7533) + utf8-source-01.t rows 42-46.  ir-spec Â§3.2h.
